title: Hypoelliptic weak Poincaré inequality with arbitrarily small L2 error for nonnegative zero-source kinetic Fokker–Planck subsolutions
source_title: Quantitative De Giorgi methods in kinetic theory
author: Jessica Guerand; Clément Mouhot
difficulty_reason: A usual Poincare inequality in velocity does not connect the separated kinetic cylinders or control position oscillations at merely measurable diffusion regularity. The Proposition13 proof constructs a four-part kinetic trajectory and uses fractional spatial regularization to make its position leg meaningful. A nonsingular position/velocity change then permits the distributional integration by parts and closes the adjustable L2 error; these nonroutine steps remain after standard energy foundations are allowed.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Selected zero-source S=0 specialization of independent Proposition13, not the general displayed source-dependent version. Exact nonnegative renormalized weak subsolution of kinetic divergence-form Fokker–Planck on Q5, measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic A and bounded measurable drift B, all epsilon in(0,1), sigma in(0,1/3), positive-part L1 deviation over future Q1 from past Q1-minus mean bounded by epsilon^(-d-2) velocity-gradient L1 plus epsilon^sigma/(1/3-sigma) L2 error. Full new fractional fundamental-kernel localization7–11 and four-trajectory/diffeomorphism/weak integration core13–16 read. With S=0, I33 vanishes exactly; the general printed proposition places its source term inside the small epsilon error although its proof gives unweighted I33, so that broader statement is excluded without supplying a new estimate. Boundary cutoff error is printed epsilon^(2d) on13, but its already displayed Cauchy–Schwarz collar error is bounded by epsilon^sigma for sigma<1/3; only the stated final epsilon^sigma term is retained. Previously published Kolmogorov fundamental solution, unimodular Young inequality and standard dyadic multiplier bounds are named foundations with authored new fractional decomposition included. No quantitative intermediate-value/Harnack/Hölder consequence or multiple parameter cases counted.
